swarm_review.finding: The Claude ingest supports dynamic context-dependent binding/routing as a training objective while positive cross-checkpoint J-Space labels remain forbidden.
The 432-row order-crossed generator removes deterministic codebook-position leakage by fully crossing six display orders, but it has no independent query-polarity axis.
A successor must cross semantic target x opaque code x query polarity with exact counts. Presence of both polarity forms is insufficient if their counts remain class-correlated.

The 96-row generator's hard-negative target form 'REJECT <wrong>; CORRECT <right>' is intentionally different from the one-symbol production contract. Do not blindly mix those rows into the same direct symbol-only SFT objective; keep them in a separately typed rejection/evaluator family or use a separately preregistered compatible objective.

Both generators correctly remain abstract. No train-ready atom rows may be minted until the accepted 46-atom inventory, exact selected-checkpoint tokenizer identity, single-token counts/positions, ABI member/row integrity and generator source identity are verified.

The 432 rows strengthen TRAIN template generation but do not establish validation/holdout lexical-family isolation, unseen-symbol holdout, or a frozen unseen-template family at final materialized-corpus scope.

Keep the order-crossed 432-row generator as the stronger current donor for binding-template construction. Add polarity/split/materialization in a separately versioned successor rather than opening a competing generator lane.

successor_design_constraint.query_polarity_rule: Exact count balance is mandatory. For a three-class task, do not treat negation as a single complement class. Use the already preregistered query-polarity construction or freeze a new unambiguous formulation before generation.
